key_insight: The paper proposes Agent-Native Immune System (ANIS), an endogenous defense framework embedded in an agent's runtime cognition to protect against hijacking, poisoning, and protocol attacks.
engineering_relevance: ANIS reframes agent security as an always-on internal control layer, complementing alignment with runtime immunity for autonomous tools, memory, and multi-agent systems.
method: Defines a six-layer Immune Tower (L0-L5), including a physical/logical Barrier Immunity layer.
Introduces a taxonomy of Agent Viruses and Agent Vaccines, distinguishing parametric vaccines from superficial defenses.
Uses a Harness Triad (Meta, Self, Auto) to support continual immune learning and adaptive response.
evidence_signal: The abstract is conceptual and architectural, emphasizing a theoretical framework and open evaluation needs rather than reporting experimental results or benchmark numbers.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is avoiding autoimmunity and false-positive interventions that could disrupt normal agent behavior and tool use.
paper_title: Agent-Native Immune System: Architecture, Taxonomy, and Engineering
